snippet.title: Behind The Making Of WEDNESDAY
snippet.description:
Today we’re going behind the scenes of Netflix’s Wednesday, starring Jenna Ortega as the titular character herself, as well as Christina Ricci, the OG Wednesday Addams. This show is already a piece of iconic media in the making with the legendary Tim Burton behind the lens. Tim Burton designed the character with sketches! He would bring different sketches of characters and monsters to the writer’s room and everyone would have a bit of input on what the characters would look like. Apparently, it was a major collaborative process all around. Jenna Ortega was extremely dedicated to perfecting her role as Wednesday and put in the long hours to show it! She was easily working twelve hours a day on set alone – not even counting her commute or the time she was in hair and makeup. She also learned to play the cello and how to fence specifically so she could perform her own stunts. She spent a non-stop eight months working! There are also some very particular mannerisms that only super keen eyes would be able to see. Like, did you know that Wednesday never blinks? She also has incredible posture and keeps her arms and hands pretty stationary most of the time. Jenna brought a lot of subtlety and care into the portrayal of this character. This show was also filmed in Romania, which brought a unique, Eastern European vibe to the show that we don’t often get to see in media. What was your favorite Wednesday moment? Let us know in the comments!

We’re looking into everything that went into the making of Guillermo del Toro’s Pinocchio! This work of stop motion animation was nearly fifteen years in the making, meaning that Guillermo del Toro has spent roughly half of his career working on it! His passion for the project most likely comes from the fact that he and his mother bonded over the Walt Disney adaptation of Pinocchio when he was a child, and so it’s come to be an extremely special story for him throughout his lifetime. Guillermo del Toro’s Pinocchio features a star-studded cast, with newcomer Gregory Mann taking on the role of Pinocchio. Finn Wolfhard of Stranger Things fame has been cast in the role of Candlewick. Tilda Swinton, who’s proven her acting chops as a member of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, plays both the ethereal Wood Sprite (here meant to serve the role of the Blue Fairy), as well as her eerier sister Death. Fellow alumni of the Marvel Cinematic Universe as well as Lord of the Rings, Cate Blanchett, plays La Colombe. David Bradley, best known for his role in Harry Potter, will be portraying the voice of Geppetto. Ewan McGregor, who plays The Talking Cricket, will be singing in this role, and this is not the first time he has flexed his musical talents in a film, as he has previously appeared in the live action remake for Disney’s Beauty and the Beast. Ron Perlman, portraying Podesta, has worked with Guillermo del Toro on several projects in the past, including Hellboy and Pacific Rim.

snippet.title: Behind The Magic of Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
snippet.description:
Let’s talk about Marvel Phase Four’s Black Panther Wakanda Forever. Director and co-writer, Ryan Coogler really struggled with the loss of his hero, Chadwick Boseman. He ended up having to rewrite the entire script due to his absence, which was an emotionally difficult process for the entire cast. He ended up writing the story through Letitia Wright’s character, Shuri’s perspective. Not only was Letitia Wright one of Chadwick Boseman’s favorite performers to work with, but the loss of his character would have definitely hit her the hardest. She ended up dedicating every aspect of her performance to him, and everyone took honoring his character very seriously. Aside from that, there were a lot of challenges to overcome when bringing this film together. For one, there were dozens of underwater scenes – the cast spent eight hours a day filming in a huge water tank. Here’s the kicker – most everyone couldn’t swim! They all either had to learn how to swim from scratch, or learn how to swim well enough to stay in the water for that long. Even Ryan Coogler had to learn! There was also a pretty serious on-set injury. Letitita Wright took a pretty severe tumble and ended up in the hospital with a fractured shoulder and a concussion. Filming had to be paused for over two months while she recovered. Avatar is a movie you can watch again and again and again. Why? Because it is so full of the tiniest possible details that made this movie such a success! Training required shooting weapons in weird ways. The animal sounds for the film were ripped off of another classic movie. However, James Cameron’s script was not. He has years of proof dating all the way back to high school! The tall blue people have always been an idea in his mind. The six-limbed creatures came later but they required completely reinventing the anatomy of every creature. Avatar changed the face of the film industry forever thanks to his high-tech inventions! They were also inventing their own style of music, doing their best not to make it sound human at all!
